import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_45/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_45/test_1.csv"
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_45/target_multisource_cot.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Source0 schema: ['State', 'Participation', 'English', 'Math', 'Reading', 'Science', 'Composite']
# Source1 schema: ['State', 'Participation', 'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing', 'Math', 'Total']

# Target schema:
# ['State': string,
#  'Participation_x': string,
#  'English': float,
#  'Math_x': float,
#  'Reading': float,
#  'Science': float,
#  'Composite': float,
#  'Participation_y': string,
#  'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing': integer,
#  'Math_y': integer,
#  'Total': integer]

# Transformation plan:
# - df0 has detailed subject scores and Participation (to be renamed Participation_x)
# - df1 has Participation (to be renamed Participation_y), Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, Math, Total
# - Join df0 and df1 on 'State' to combine all columns
# - Rename columns accordingly:
#     - df0.Participation -> Participation_x
#     - df0.Math -> Math_x (float)
#     - df1.Participation -> Participation_y
#     - df1.Math -> Math_y (integer)
# - Ensure data types match target schema:
#     - Participation_x, Participation_y: string (keep as is)
#     - English, Math_x, Reading, Science, Composite: float
#     - Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, Math_y, Total: integer
# - Some states may appear in one source but not the other; use inner join to keep only states present in both sources (target examples show states present in both)
# - After join, reorder columns to match target schema

# Rename columns in df0 and df1 before join to avoid confusion
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={
    'Participation': 'Participation_x',
    'Math': 'Math_x'
})

df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={
    'Participation': 'Participation_y',
    'Math': 'Math_y'
})

# Join on 'State' (inner join to keep only states present in both)
df_merged = pd.merge(df0_renamed, df1_renamed, on='State', how='inner')

# Convert data types to match target schema
# Participation_x and Participation_y are strings with % sign, keep as string
# English, Math_x, Reading, Science, Composite: float
float_cols = ['English', 'Math_x', 'Reading', 'Science', 'Composite']
for col in float_cols:
    df_merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged[col], errors='coerce')

# Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, Math_y, Total: integer
int_cols = ['Evidence-Based Reading and Writing', 'Math_y', 'Total']
for col in int_cols:
    df_merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'State',
    'Participation_x',
    'English',
    'Math_x',
    'Reading',
    'Science',
    'Composite',
    'Participation_y',
    'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing',
    'Math_y',
    'Total'
]

df_target = df_merged[target_columns]

# Save to CSV without the index
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
